standard.title: Create works that communicate ideas
standard.description: create arts works that communicate ideas
standard.prior_knowledge: No formal prior arts learning assumed. Students bring play, curiosity and informal experience with voice, movement and sound from early childhood. This is their first formal encounter with creating arts works within a school context.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students create arts works in at least one form that communicate ideas from personal experience, using deliberate choices about how the work will look, sound or feel.

nodes.label: Ideas from experience as starting points
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify a personal experience or idea as the starting point for an arts work and describe what they want to communicate.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one personal experience (e.g. a favourite activity or a feeling) and describe what they want to show or express.
nodes.typical_width: Draw on personal or social experiences, play, imagination or observation as starting points; name what they want to communicate — e.g. 'I want to show how running feels' or 'I want to tell the story of my pet.'
wider: Draw on literature, artworks or stories from their culture as starting points — compare how their idea connects to or differs from the source
Use dramatic play scenarios as starting points for both musical and visual ideas — ask 'What could the sound of this story be?'
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot identify a personal idea or intent before making will produce work without communicative purpose. The next phase — making deliberate choices in a form — requires a starting intention. Without it, students move through the activity without the central act of the descriptor being engaged.

response_modes.reason: Use questioning to help students articulate their starting idea before they begin making — 'What do you want to show?', 'Who is this for?', 'What should people feel when they see/hear it?' This scaffolds the intent-setting that the rest of the making depends on.

success_criteria: Can name one personal experience or idea they want to communicate in their arts work
Can describe (in any form — drawing, speaking, gesturing) what they want the work to show or express

nodes.label: Choosing an arts form
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can choose an arts form (voice/music, movement, drawing, dramatic play) that suits the idea they want to communicate.
nodes.minimum_width: Attempt to create in at least one arts form (e.g. a chant, a drawing, or a movement sequence) with a connection to their intended idea.
nodes.typical_width: Try communicating an idea across two or more arts forms; notice how each form communicates differently — e.g. a chant communicates rhythm and energy while a drawing communicates visual detail.
wider: Compare how the same idea (e.g. 'the ocean') could be communicated through voice/sound vs movement vs image — make a choice and explain it
Use digital devices (e.g. camera or recording app) to capture and compare attempts in different forms

response_modes.reason: Students need exposure to the full range of arts forms available to them before they can make informed choices. Ensuring students have tried voice/sound, movement and image-making contexts builds the repertoire from which genuine choice becomes possible.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Comparing how the same idea communicates differently across forms is genuinely rich at Foundation — it surfaces the idea that form shapes meaning, which is foundational to all arts learning.
success_criteria: Attempts to create in at least one arts form with a recognisable connection to their intended idea
Can say something about why they chose that form or what it shows about their idea

nodes.label: Making deliberate choices in the work
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can make at least one deliberate decision during the making process (e.g. changing a word, adding a movement, choosing a sound) and connect it to their communicative intent.
nodes.minimum_width: Make one deliberate change or decision during the making process; describe why they made it.
nodes.typical_width: Extend and vary known songs, chants or rhymes through deliberate choices (changing words, adding movements, improvising accompaniments); use play and experimentation to try options and select preferred ones.
wider: Use an available digital device to record work in progress, listen back and make a decision about what to change or keep
Devise a chant or rap with a specific message in mind — make deliberate decisions about rhythm and words to carry the message
nodes.hinge_reason: Deliberate choice-making — however simple — is the difference between executing an activity and making an arts work. If students do not practise connecting decisions to intent at Foundation, the later demands of composition and performance (which require iterative decision-making) begin without this foundational habit established.

response_modes.reason: Pause during making to ask simple reflective questions: 'Why did you put that there?', 'What would happen if you changed it?', 'Does it still show your idea?' These questions build the habit of connecting decisions to intent.

success_criteria: Makes at least one deliberate decision during the making process (not just following a template)
Can describe the decision and connect it in some way to what they wanted to communicate

nodes.label: Completing and sharing a work
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can complete a simple arts work that communicates an intended idea and share it with peers or teacher.
nodes.minimum_width: Complete an arts work (in any form) that has a recognisable communicative intent; share it with at least one other person.
nodes.typical_width: Complete arts works across two or more forms; share them via a gallery walk, informal performance, or digital capture; respond to questions about the work such as 'What is happening in your work?' or 'What did you want to show?'
wider: Create a multi-form work (e.g. a chant combined with a drawing) that communicates one idea across two forms simultaneously
Use a digital device to record and share a composed chant or soundscape — curate a simple image sequence to accompany it

response_modes.reason: This node is where intent, form choice and deliberate decisions come together in a finished, sharable work. The teaching investment is in supporting students to see their work as complete and communicating — not just as an activity they did.

success_criteria: Produces a completed arts work (in any form) that communicates a recognisable idea
Can talk about what the work is meant to show or express when asked
